content: (The location is now Haelga's Bunkhouse.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Svana Far-Shield, Grelka, Gilen, Niluva Hlaalu) (MJR: Why don't you wear some of these items...? (Persuade); Haelga: Okay. Just this once.)

Haelga: Fine, fine, I'll put on the amulet of Dibella you gave me, but only because it's blessed by the goddess herself. Madesi: That is a wise choice, Haelga. Dibella's favor brings fortune to any enterprise. Lydia: Amulets and trinkets are nothing compared to the strength of a good blade. Still, if it pleases my thane, I will not object. Tythis Ulen: Amulets or not, I hope you didn't forget the key to the storage room. I need to lock up my catch before bed.

Haelga: The night is still young, and I have honey and mead ready for anyone who wants to stay and share in Dibella's blessings. Madesi: I should return to my stall at dawn, but a warm cup of mead sounds inviting. Your honey always has a special touch, Haelga. Lydia: The only honey I need is the thrill of battle and the warmth of my thane's favor. These soft beds make warriors weak. Tythis Ulen: Some of us work the docks all day, Lydia. A soft bed and a willing hand are exactly what we need. Svana, would you fetch me a drink?

Haelga: By Dibella's grace, Madesi, what are you doing? Not that I mind the view, but customers might get the wrong idea. Madesi: The night air is warm, and my scales need to breathe after a long day haggling in the market. Let them stare if they wish. Lydia: An Argonian shedding his skin like a snake in a bunkhouse. Disgusting. Cover yourself before I mistake you for a target. Tythis Ulen: Easy, Lydia. Madesi's a good sort. Besides, it's his own hide he's airing out. Brand-Shei, did you see that statue our thane just picked up?

Haelga: You... you took my gold and my dignity in one breath. May Dibella forgive you, because I cannot forget this night. Madesi: That was a harsh price for a simple statue, friend. Haelga has always been generous to travelers and merchants alike. Tythis Ulen: Easy, Madesi. Our thane has his reasons, I'm sure. Though I'll admit, shaking down a landlady over a holy symbol leaves a sour taste in my mouth. Lydia: The thane took what was owed. If Haelga values her goddess so much, she should guard her treasures better.

Haelga: I need some air. And a fresh bottle of mead. Perhaps several. Goodnight to all who still call me friend. Madesi: Rest well, Haelga. The dawn brings new customers and new fortunes. Tythis Ulen: I think I'll turn in as well. The docks start early tomorrow. Svana, lock up after me. Lydia: Finally, some quiet. The thane and I have important business at first light.
Madesi: I think this night has run its course. I wish you all peaceful dreams. Tythis Ulen: Aye, my bones ache for rest. Goodnight, everyone. Lydia: Finally. Some of us have real work in the morning.

Haelga: Well then. The fire's dying and so is this conversation. I suppose we've all had enough excitement for one night. Madesi: Indeed. The candle burns low and my eyes grow heavy. Perhaps tomorrow will bring better fortunes. Tythis Ulen: There's nothing left to say that won't keep until morning. Let the silence have its turn. Lydia: Good. Less talk means fewer foolish ideas.
